extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary and secondary schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX compliance for educational recipients
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and regulatory requirements that recipients of federal education funding must follow to prevent, investigate, and remedy sex discrimination (including sex-based harassment), and to adopt grievance procedures, training, recordkeeping, and related administrative practices consistent with 34 CFR part 106 final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to adopt grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Require recipients to adopt grievance procedures that provide for fair, prompt, and equitable resolution of complaints of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations strengthen recipients' obligations to provide prompt and equitable grievance procedures and to take other necessary steps when they receive a complaint of sex discrimination; additional, specific requirements apply at postsecondary institutions for complaints of sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or student respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'sex-based harassment'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'sex-based harassment' as a form of sex discrimination that includes sexual harassment and harassment based on sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, or gender identity, that is quid pro quo harassment, hostile environment harassment, or one of four specific Clery Act–referenced offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition clarifies what conduct falls within Title IX's prohibition and ties listed offenses to the Clery Act definitions (as amended by VAWA 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of sex discrimination (protected characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that sex discrimination includes discrimination on the basis of sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations and preamble explain recipients' obligations not to discriminate based on these bases and indicate reliance on case law (e.g., Bostock) and other authorities to interpret coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of pregnancy and parental status
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the terms 'pregnancy or related conditions' and 'parental status' for regulatory purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions are used to clarify treatment of students and employees who are pregnant or parenting and to inform regulatory protections and required recipient actions (e.g., reasonable modifications, lactation space, voluntary leaves).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on pregnancy/parental discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits discrimination against students, applicants for admission, employees, or applicants for employment on the basis of current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations clarify recipients' obligations to provide information, reasonable modifications, voluntary leave options, access to comparable program portions, limits on supporting documentation, and certification requirements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Title IX Coordinator (§106.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must designate a Title IX Coordinator responsible for coordinating the recipient's compliance with Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble highlights streamlining administrative requirements and clarifies Title IX Coordinator responsibilities (see §106.44(f) and other sections for coordinator duties such as duty to monitor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination policy, grievance procedures, and notice (§106.8(b) & (c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt and disseminate a nondiscrimination policy, maintain grievance procedures, and provide a notice of nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are administrative requirements aimed at ensuring the campus community knows how to report and how the recipient will handle complaints; see Document Drafting Handbook for more details on paperwork and citation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train a range of relevant persons on the recipient's obligations under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations specify recipient training obligations and the Regulatory Impact Analysis references training for decisionmakers (§106.46(f)(4)). Training should reflect recipients' obligations to provide fair processes and to evaluate evidence objectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements (§106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain records as required by the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping supports oversight and accountability; the Regulatory Impact Analysis specifically notes recordkeeping (§106.8(f)) as an area of cost and compliance consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to operate program/activity free from sex discrimination (§106.44 general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are obligated to operate their education program or activity free from sex discrimination, including taking actions to prevent and address sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general duty encompasses monitoring for barriers, notification requirements, supportive measures, public awareness, and other actions described throughout §106.44.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for barriers (§106.44(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have a duty to monitor for barriers to equal participation and access and take action to address them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinator obligations include the duty to monitor; monitoring is treated as part of a recipient's operational duties to prevent sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must meet specified notification requirements when addressing sex discrimination complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification requirements relate to informing parties about processes, supportive measures, rights, and available resources, and are detailed in §106.44(c) and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee / confidentiality provisions (sections 106.2 and 106.44(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain confidentiality or 'confidential employee' requirements and definitions apply and limit mandatory reporting in some circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble cross-references definitions and recipient obligations; recipients must understand which employees qualify as confidential and how that affects reporting and investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures (§106.44(f)-(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide supportive measures to complainants and others as appropriate to ensure access to educational opportunities pending resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures should be prompt and effective; §106.44(g)(4) emphasizes impartial review of supportive measures; §106.45(l) lists ranges of supportive measures and disciplinary sanctions and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal and administrative leave (§106.44(h)-(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations permit emergency removal of a respondent and administrative leave in certain circumstances, subject to procedural protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removal must comply with due process requirements; §106.45(h)(4) requires complying with grievance procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited disclosures of personally identifiable information (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are restricted from making certain disclosures of personally identifiable information about parties and must follow privacy protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interacts with FERPA and other privacy laws; recipients must limit sharing information consistent with statutory and regulatory privacy protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution process (§106.44(k) and §106.46(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide for an informal resolution process as an option in some cases, subject to voluntary participation and appropriate safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not coerce parties into informal resolution; the preamble notes instances where informal resolution should not be pushed and that some complainants did not wish to pursue informal routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedural fairness and equity (§106.45(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must treat complainants and respondents equitably throughout the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity obligations include neutral procedures, timely timeframes, and balanced access to evidence, advisors, and opportunities to present witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and bias protections (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must have procedures to address conflicts of interest or bias (including discouraging single-investigator models in some contexts) to ensure impartial investigations and adjudications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses commenters' concerns about presumptions of guilt and conflict; §106.46(f)(4) addresses training for decisionmakers, and the Regulatory Impact Analysis references single-investigator model considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of innocence until determination (§106.45(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged sex discrimination until a determination is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption must be respected in the recipient's procedures and communications; other procedural protections (e.g., impartial evaluation of evidence) support this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of evidence and exclusion of impermissible evidence (§106.45(b)(6)-(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must provide for objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and the exclusion of impermissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure investigators and decisionmakers assess relevance and admissibility, provide access to relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence (§106.45(f)(3)-(4), §106.46(e)(6)), and permit opportunities to present witnesses and other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes and timely process (§106.45(b)(6), §106.46(e)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include reasonable timeframes for major stages of the process, promoting prompt resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses commenters' concerns about lengthy processes; regulations require timeframes for investigations, notice, and determinations and allow some flexibility consistent with equitable and prompt resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof and notification of determination (§106.45(h)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must identify the standard of proof and require notification of the determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directed questions on the standard of proof are addressed in the preamble; recipients must notify parties of outcomes and provide information on remedies and appeals (§106.45(h)(3), (i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies, sanctions, and limitation on discipline (§106.45(h)(3)-(5), §106.45(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide remedies to complainants and take appropriate steps; disciplinary sanctions must comply with procedures and there is a prohibition on imposing discipline based solely on the determination without other required steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations require recipients to comply with grievance procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions and to avoid disciplining solely on the finding without appropriate procedural protections; §106.45(l) lists ranges of supportive measures and disciplinary sanctions and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to relevant evidence and parties' ability to review (§106.45(f)(2)-(4), §106.46(e)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must have access to relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence, and opportunity to review evidence and present witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This access is balanced with privacy and evidentiary exclusions; recipients must provide mechanisms for parties to review evidence and respond during investigations and adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary-specific procedural protections (§106.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: For sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or respondent at postsecondary institutions, additional requirements apply including written notice of allegations, advance notice of meetings, role of advisor, other persons present at proceedings, expert witnesses, timeframes, access to evidence, evaluating allegations, and live hearings (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46 enumerates extra procedural protections for postsecondary contexts; the preamble explains these are intended to better protect students and ensure fairness in campus adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings for postsecondary complaints (§106.46(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide for live hearings in certain postsecondary grievance processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live hearings are described among postsecondary-specific provisions and are tied to notice, advisor roles, and rules for who may be present; the preamble addresses concerns and operational issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and additional provisions (§106.45(i), §106.46(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations require that grievance procedures include an appeals process and other additional procedural provisions to ensure fairness and finality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be made available consistent with principles of equity and must be described in recipients' grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretary review (§106.47)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for Assistant Secretary review of certain Title IX decisions or processes under the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.47 creates a higher-level review mechanism within the Department for addressing issues of compliance and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation prohibition and definition (§106.71 and §106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits retaliation against individuals engaging in protected activity; defines retaliation in terms of protected activity, adverse action, and causal connection, and provides examples and intersections with grievance-procedure provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble discusses examples of prohibited retaliation, intersections with §106.45(h)(5), First Amendment considerations, and requests to clarify or modify text; recipients must address retaliation claims promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis harm standard for sex-based separations (§106.31(a) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that, except as permitted by Title IX/regulations, recipients must not carry out different treatment or separation on the basis of sex in a way that would cause more than de minimis harm, including policies that prevent participation consistent with gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The de minimis harm standard limits recipients' ability to justify sex-based separations or treatment; the preamble notes intersections with parental rights, health care, religious beliefs, appearance codes, juvenile justice facilities, and burden on schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of party, complainant, and respondent (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'complainant' (a person alleged to have been subjected to conduct that could constitute sex discrimination), 'respondent' (a person alleged to have violated prohibition), and 'party' (complainant or respondent), including situations where a parent/guardian/legal representative acts on behalf of an individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions apply throughout 34 CFR part 106 and inform who has rights and responsibilities under the regulations; preamble clarifies usage and cross-references §106.6(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and interaction with other laws and statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations and preamble clarify interactions with other civil rights laws and statutes (FERPA, GEPA/FERPA, ADA, IDEA, Title VII, Clery Act, VAWA, HIPAA) and preserve rights provided by other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble discusses consistency with other civil rights laws OCR enforces, effect of other requirements, preservation of rights, and intersections (e.g., FERPA limits on disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and regulatory process standards (commenting, effective dates, RIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes rulemaking process elements: length of public comment period, process for submitting/posting comments, effective date (final regs effective Aug 1, 2024), Regulatory Impact Analysis topics (costs, benefits, alternatives), and considerations like Regulatory Flexibility Act impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble explains timing, changes from the NPRM, number of comments received, directed questions, and that the RIA addresses costs/benefits, small business impacts, and accounting statements; effective date chosen to allow recipients time to plan implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions addressing pregnancy/parenting accommodations and lactation (§106.40, §106.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take specific actions to prevent discrimination and ensure equal access for individuals with pregnancy or related conditions, including information responsibilities, reasonable modifications, voluntary program access, voluntary leaves of absence, lactation space/time, and limitations on supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate sections address student protections (§106.40) and employee protections (§106.57), including return-from-leave, comparable treatment to other temporary medical conditions, and pre-employment inquiries (§106.60).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public awareness, data collection, and climate surveys (§106.44(e), miscellaneous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are encouraged or required to engage in public awareness events and may be involved in data collection and climate surveys to assess and address sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble lists public awareness and data/collection topics as part of recipient responsibilities and OCR enforcement practices; these support prevention and monitoring efforts.
